# Native Multi-DOF Manifold BoxFDDP Candidate (Provisional)

## Admitted Plant and Information Pattern

F05d (#11932, parent F05 #11789) uses the F05c synthetic MuJoCo 3.8.0
floating-root, two-hinge plant. The pelvis root has no actuator; only the
hip and knee receive named, direct unit-gain motors. The contact-free,
gravity-free model has no plugin, tendon, muscle activation, equality
constraint, hidden gravity compensation or external force. The exact
native Euler step is $h=0.01\,\mathrm{s}$, with $n_q=9$, $n_v=8$,
$n_u=2$. The controller reads the exact simulated $(q,v)$ at each native
step and cannot use future observations. The independently replayed plant
starts from complete `mjSTATE_INTEGRATION`, including numerical state;
the replay receives only the saved, post-limit ZOH motor torques and no
controller or observations. This is an exact-state synthetic experiment,
not a measured golfer or motion-capture comparison.

## Manifold Dynamics, Cost and Admission

The Crocoddyl state has $n_x=17$ physical numbers and $n_{\delta x}=16$
local numbers. Its configuration difference and retraction call MuJoCo's
`mj_differentiatePos` and `mj_integratePos`; the root quaternion in native
$(w,x,y,z)$ order is never subtracted or incremented as four Euclidean
components. The configuration is normalized at admission, and $q$ and
$-q$ give the same local orientation error. State-operation Jacobians use
centered tangent perturbations of $10^{-6}$; identity-point derivative
tests confirm the expected $(-I,I)$ difference and $(I,I)$ integration
limits. [Crocoddyl's state contract](https://gepettoweb.laas.fr/doc/loco-3d/crocoddyl/master/doxygen-html/classcrocoddyl_1_1StateNumDiffTpl.html)
distinguishes state and tangent dimensions, and
[MuJoCo's computation reference](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.8.0/computation.html#derivatives)
defines the discrete native derivative.

Each Crocoddyl action advances the same native $x_{k+1}=F_h(x_k,u_k)$ as
execution. The action derivative is the F05c native Euler
`mjd_transitionFD` $A_k\in\mathbb R^{16\times16}$,
$B_k\in\mathbb R^{16\times2}$, checked against an independent stepped
state. At each stage, with $e_{k+1}=\operatorname{diff}(x^*_{k+1},x_{k+1})$,
the cost is

$$
\ell_k=e_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}W e_{k+1}+u_k^{\mathsf T}R u_k,
\qquad \ell_T=e_T^{\mathsf T}(3W)e_T.
$$

The fixed synthetic weights are $W=(1,1,1,1,1,1,20,20,
0.1,\ldots,0.1)$ on root translation (m), root rotation (rad), two
hinge angles (rad) and eight velocities (native SI), with
$R=\operatorname{diag}(0.01,0.01)$ for motor torques (N m). They are
optimization weights, not inferred human physiology. Cost derivatives
use the manifold error Jacobian and a Gauss–Newton positive semidefinite
approximation; native $A_k,B_k$ retain coupling and unactuated-root
response. The input box is the compiled motor `ctrlrange`, tightened by
$10^{-4}\,\mathrm{N\,m}$ on each side so centered control derivatives
remain inside the native clamp. The solver has a four-step horizon,
15-iteration cap and a predeclared cooperative 0.2 s call budget. The
budget is checked after the call returns and does **not** promise a hard
deadline. The fixture does not impose anatomical joint or contact-state
bounds; state feasibility here means finite, normalized, contact-free
native steps.

The first proposed command is applied only when the solver succeeds within
that budget, its whole input plan stays in the native box, and a fresh
nonlinear native rollout of the entire plan improves the identical
reference/effort objective over the zero-torque fallback. A rejected,
timed-out, stale, cancelled, exceptional or non-improving proposal yields
the verified fallback and discards the warm plan. The compiled model
identity, callback absence, actuator order, model topology, contact
policy and native integrator are checked before control. A different
loaded execution model rejects. This independent admission matters even
when a bounded optimizer reports success.

## Paired Development Measurement and Limits

The source-hashed receipt
`docs/development/feedback_controls/F05D_NATIVE_MANIFOLD_RECEIPT_MJ38.json`
uses the same synthetic model, exact initial native state, a moving
reference generated by native steps with a fixed admissible teacher input,
reference, torque bounds, four-step horizon, 15-iteration cap, 0.2 s
cooperative call budget and **same native nonlinear acceptance cost** for
Crocoddyl BoxFDDP and SciPy SLSQP shooting. The two starts are hip
$0.4$ and $0.7\,\mathrm{rad}$; solver order reverses between them. Both
paths independently export actual held motor commands through the pinned
Tools T01 contract and replay the complete native integration-state
trajectory to $10^{-12}$. A common Tools preflight is timed and charged
to both; each run also includes solver preparation, every accepted or
fallback call, native execution, export and independent replay. Process
launch and test collection are outside the measured interval.

The recorded 0.2 s fixture admits three of eight BoxFDDP commands across
the two starts and no SciPy commands. Timed-out solves apply the verified
zero-torque fallback. Both methods have **null time to a fully accepted
run** under this budget. BoxFDDP's realized native cost is lower in both
starts (31.93 versus 254.35 and 61.80 versus 201.83), even though five
of its calls time out; the exact per-call statuses and variable wall times
remain in the receipt. This is a fixture-specific improvement in executed
tracking, not a deadline or solver-selection result. F02 TVLQR remains
the broader default. It does not
establish a 10 ms deadline, robustness to uncertain contact, anatomic
or muscle control, private-capture matching, full-body swing behavior,
six-engine parity or a production solver selection. Parent F05 and
manual publication remain blocked.
